description: Correctness Review adversarial host-observation rubrics with reproducible Git fixtures; catalog validation is not model-performance evidence

cases.scenario: Boundary count permits a third refund
cases.input: Prepare this fixture as a disposable Git repository using evals/review/build_correctness_fixtures.py --case CR-01; review only its frozen base/head with docs/accepted-behavior.md as the stated source. Preserve exact file:line evidence, inspect both versions and distinguish confirmed defect from ambiguity or a correct change.

fixture.contract:
# Approved BR-REFUND
A user with exactly two completed refunds during the last 365 days must not receive another refund. The function receives the already-completed refund count.

checks.criterion: Identifies completed_refunds=2 as the reachable boundary violation, citing BR-REFUND and the modified guard
States expected rejection versus actual acceptance and the concrete third-refund consequence
Does not claim the presence of tests or a successful run without inspected execution evidence

cases.scenario: Boolean precedence bypasses a required activity guard
cases.input: Prepare this fixture as a disposable Git repository using evals/review/build_correctness_fixtures.py --case CR-03; review only its frozen base/head with docs/accepted-behavior.md as the stated source. Preserve exact file:line evidence, inspect both versions and distinguish confirmed defect from ambiguity or a correct change.

fixture.contract:
# Approved BR-ACCESS
A command is allowed only when the account is active AND the actor is either an administrator or the resource owner.
fixture.base:
def allowed(active, admin, owner):
    return active and (admin or owner)
fixture.changed:
def allowed(active, admin, owner):
    return active and admin or owner

checks.criterion: Identifies active=False and owner=True as a concrete reachable bypass due to operator precedence
Explains the approved active-account precondition and how the new expression violates it
Does not treat the mere use of an or expression as a finding without a concrete branch witness

cases.scenario: Semi-open time interval endpoints are reversed
cases.input: Prepare this fixture as a disposable Git repository using evals/review/build_correctness_fixtures.py --case CR-06; review only its frozen base/head with docs/accepted-behavior.md as the stated source. Preserve exact file:line evidence, inspect both versions and distinguish confirmed defect from ambiguity or a correct change.

fixture.contract:
# Approved BR-WINDOW
An event belongs to the window exactly when start <= event_time < end. The caller supplies timestamps on one comparable time basis.
fixture.base:
def in_window(event_time, start, end):
    return start <= event_time < end
fixture.changed:
def in_window(event_time, start, end):
    return start < event_time <= end

checks.criterion: Identifies both exact endpoints as changed from the approved semi-open interval
Provides a concrete counterexample for event_time=start or event_time=end
Does not invent timezone or daylight-saving errors when this fixture fixes a common time basis

fixture.contract:
